clue.text: He'll go to bed with you, but his involvement is strictly financial

definitions.text: He'll go to bed with you
definitions.meaning: a bedfellow, the person who shares your bed at night
a business investor who puts in money but takes no part in running the firm

explanation.surface: A lover whose interest in the relationship turns out to be purely about money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: a literal bedfellow, and the British business term for a silent investor in a partnership.

clue.text: Bug ranges around India, at first having travelled rapidly on the air

indicators.note: the spans go around the letter for India

parts.note: spans are ranges
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: only the first letter of having is used
on the air means broadcast, so spoken

parts.note: flew means travelled rapidly

explanation.surface: A virus spread quickly by airborne transmission across India.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is an infectious illness; this was the 1918 influenza pandemic.

clue.text: Supply nurse with what's owed

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
something due is owed

explanation.surface: Pay a nurse the wages she is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow or provide someone with a quality, a formal verb for furnish.

clue.text: Question related to coach's raw material before transformation?

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them for information
kin are relatives, people related to you

explanation.surface: A query about what a carriage is made of before it was changed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cinderella the fairy godmother turns a vegetable into a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale coach began as this vegetable, so it is the raw material in the story.

clue.text: Inflexible upstart controlling national government ultimately, yet with power to give briefings like this?

indicators.note: controlling means holding, so the reversed word holds the others
start going up, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: iron means unyielding or inflexible
NAT is a short form of national

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of government

parts.note: yet means but
able means having the power or capability

explanation.surface: A rigid new official in charge of government who can brief the press anonymously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give' is a link. 'upstart' looks like a noun for a parvenu, but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-record press briefings cannot be quoted with a source named, the typical journalism usage.

clue.text: Deferral of favourable credit on wine country

parts.note: pro means in favour
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Putting off a good loan secured on a vineyard region.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual delay, putting off doing things until later.

clue.text: Collect drinks cheerfully

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
up means in good spirits

explanation.surface: Go and fetch the drinks in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together people or animals, as cattle are herded in.

clue.text: Day out in Edinburgh spoilt after entry of old person from one's home town?

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so the letters are jumbled
out means removed, so the letter for day goes

explanation.surface: An Edinburgh outing ruined when an old local turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after entry of' tells you O is added before the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living nearby; the question mark admits that a townsman need not be next door.

clue.text: Endless mechanical repetition's adult pattern of work

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: rote is learning by mechanical repetition
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: Rote learning sets the adult's working routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of duties showing who works which shift.

clue.text: Stomach muscle to work at, chaps

parts.note: abs are stomach muscles, one being an ab
to do a task is to work at it
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A gym instruction: exercise your stomach muscle, lads.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly region of the body, the anatomical word for the tummy area.

clue.text: Love is integral to religious sect, one helping us see the light?

definitions.text: one helping us see the light?

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: being integral to something means being built into it, so the word is goes inside the sect

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

explanation.surface: Love is central to a religious group, whose leader shows followers the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See the light' suggests religious conversion, fitting the sect, but here it is literal eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor helps patients see properly; the question mark flags the playful religious phrasing.

clue.text: Winter Olympian perhaps performing trick with ease

indicators.note: performing as in putting on a routine, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Winter Games athlete pulls off a difficult move effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Figure and speed skating are Winter Olympic sports, so a skater is an example of such an athlete.

clue.text: A carrier bearing building materials westward to Gulf metropolis

indicators.note: in an across clue, going westward means reading right to left

parts.note: a hod is a trough on a pole for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A lorry carrying construction supplies heads west towards a big city in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Qatar, a large city on the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Travel north towards rising sun's beam, having deviated from course

parts.note: to go is to travel
the sun rises in the east
a ray is a beam

explanation.surface: Heading north, then east into the sunrise, and losing the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander off the right path, an idiom for being lost or misled.

clue.text: That woman's maintaining a prohibition on salsa appearing regularly in Latin dances

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the pronoun holds the other letters

parts.note: that woman is her
a ban is a prohibition

indicators.note: only every other letter of salsa appears

explanation.surface: A woman keeps up a ban on salsa at Latin dance evenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That woman's' is 'that woman has', the 's being a link. Salsa itself is a Latin dance, a neat distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a Cuban dance in slow duple time, made famous by Carmen.

clue.text: Sausage broke apart, containing uncooked end of meat inside

indicators.note: the burst word holds the other letters

parts.note: burst means broke apart

indicators.note: the last letter goes inside the uncooked word

parts.note: raw means uncooked

indicators.note: the end of meat is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sausage split open, showing raw meat at its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A German frying sausage, usually pork.

clue.text: Italian valley enjoying opposite of cold snap

indicators.note: the valley enjoys, that is has or holds, the other word inside it

parts.note: the Po Valley is the great plain of northern Italy, named after its river
the opposite of cold is hot

explanation.surface: An Italian valley is having a heatwave after a cold spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold snap' reads as one weather phrase; 'snap' is in fact the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal word for a quick photograph.

clue.text: Did spring rental, with a parking space thrown in

indicators.note: thrown in as an extra, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: in British usage a let is a property rented out
P is the sign for a parking place

explanation.surface: Someone took a spring holiday let that came with a parking space included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did spring' looks like a season, but it is the past tense of jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb meaning to jump, as in jumped or bounded.

clue.text: Calorie-free crumpet, battered — a deep-fried speciality

indicators.note: battered means beaten about, so letters are scrambled
calorie-free means without it, so C drops out

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: A low-calorie teatime crumpet, coated in batter as a fried delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' doubles as a cooking word, fitting the Japanese dish in which food is dipped in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese dish of seafood or vegetables fried in light batter.

clue.text: Bizarre mania for stuffing cheese in slow cooker

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are used to stuff the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese

indicators.note: bizarre means strange or twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange craze for filling cheese inside a slow cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A water bath in which dishes are cooked or kept warm gently, a method of slow heating.

clue.text: Animal experimenter fed canine titbit

indicators.note: the experimenter is fed, taking in the letter

parts.note: Dr Moreau in H G Wells's novel creates beast-men by experiments
C is the dental shorthand for a canine tooth

explanation.surface: A scientist working on animals feeds a dog a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for a morsel or small piece, used in English for a short piece.

clue.text: Saw film regularly to experience immersion

indicators.note: regularly means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Watching a movie to get the immersive cinema experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Immersion' suggests an immersive film, but it is being in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving through water is to be immersed in it, the literal sense of immersion.

clue.text: Britain takes to brew around end of the afternoon on these?

indicators.note: the stirred letters go around the other two
to brew is to stew or mix, so these letters are stirred up
the end of the word the is its last letter

explanation.surface: The British habit of making a cuppa in the late afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to brew' makes TBREAKS, and 'around' wraps it round EA. The whole clue doubles as a picture of the answer, a semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Short breaks for a cup of tea are when people in Britain stop to make one.

clue.text: One scared of local spirit

parts.note: A is one
frit is a dialect word, local to parts of England, for frightened

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of a ghost from the local area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frit' is English dialect for scared, made famous by Margaret Thatcher in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabic mythology, a powerful evil demon or jinn.

clue.text: Looking up fungi's description

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue means reading upwards

parts.note: ceps are edible mushrooms

explanation.surface: Looking in a guide for a description of mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for specification, a detailed technical description.

clue.text: Volte-face by Caesar's killer leaving us and theatre in dismay

indicators.note: a volte-face is a complete about-turn, so the pieces turn round
leaving means taking away, so the word us drops out

parts.note: Brutus was among the assassins of Julius Caesar
rep, short for repertory, is a kind of theatre

explanation.surface: A U-turn by Caesar's assassin leaves us and the theatre audience aghast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs meaning to unsettle or upset someone deeply.

clue.text: National newspaper spending a million on taking control of Northern Echo mistakenly

indicators.note: taking control of means taking in, so the other letters go inside
spending a million means it is gone, so M drops out

parts.note: the Mirror is a British national daily tabloid
M is the abbreviation for million
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A national paper pays a million to buy the regional Northern Echo, wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Northern Echo is a real newspaper in north-east England, but here it splits into N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by mistake is doing it wrongly, an adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Working from home's too much in confined space, amid dirt, really exhausted

indicators.note: in means placed inside the confined space

parts.note: a cage is a confined space
OTT, over the top, means too much
amid dirt is in dust

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, so only the outer letters of really remain

explanation.surface: Working from home is too much when you are cramped, filthy and worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' is 'is', a link. OTT is British slang for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A small business carried on in workers' own houses, such as weaving or crafts.
